description: Plurals, ordinals and select (PROTOCOL.md 5.4): the ICU MessageFormat subset a `count` / `select` call renders. `text` is the stored cell, `lang` the language it is rendered in, `values` what the call passes (`count` a number, a select variable a string). `formatIcuMessage` picks the branch — an exact `=N` first, then the CLDR category of `count` in `lang` (`Intl.PluralRules`, `cardinal` for `plural`, `ordinal` for `selectordinal`), then `other`; a select picks the branch named by its value, else `other`; a block whose variable has no value falls back to `other`; `#` inside a plural branch is the number. The plain placeholders (`{count}`, `{gender}`) are NOT filled by this step: `replace` does, afterwards (`replace.json`), with `{count}` and one `{variable}` per select entry under the caller's map. `formatted` is the output of this step alone; `rendered` is the whole thing (`formatTranslation`), when it differs.
source: packages/core/message-format.ts: formatIcuMessage(text, lang, values); service.ts: formatTranslation(text, lang, options)

categories.description: `pluralCategoriesFor(lang, type)`: the CLDR categories a language uses, sorted. The API validates a model answer against exactly this set (plus any `=N`), the client relies on it to pick a branch. A runtime without `Intl.PluralRules` answers ["one", "other"] (cardinal) or ["other"] (ordinal).
